metadata.title: Scene Representation Networks: Continuous 3D-Structure-Aware Neural Scene Representations
metadata.authors: Vincent Sitzmann, Michael Zollhoefer, Gordon Wetzstein

nodes.name: Training Set of Posed Images
nodes.statement: Training set $\mathcal{C} = \{(\mathcal{I}_i, \mathbf{E}_i, \mathbf{K}_i)\}_{i=1}^N$ of $N$ tuples of images $\mathcal{I}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times 3}$ with extrinsic $\mathbf{E}_i = [\mathbf{R}|\mathbf{t}] \in \mathbb{R}^{3\times 4}$ and intrinsic $\mathbf{K}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}$ camera matrices.
nodes.statement_clean: A training dataset is a collection of 2D images each annotated with its camera intrinsic and extrinsic matrices.

nodes.name: Scene Representation Function $\Phi$
nodes.statement: A scene is represented as a continuous function $\Phi : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^n$, $\mathbf{x} \mapsto \Phi(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{v}$, mapping a spatial location to a learned feature vector $\mathbf{v}$ encoding local scene properties.
nodes.statement_clean: Phi is a continuous function from 3D world coordinates to an n-dimensional feature vector representing local scene geometry/appearance.

nodes.name: Neural Rendering Function $\Theta$
nodes.statement: Neural renderer $\Theta : \mathcal{X} \times \mathbb{R}^{3\times 4} \times \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3} \to \mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times 3}$, $(\Phi, \mathbf{E}, \mathbf{K}) \mapsto \Theta(\Phi, \mathbf{E}, \mathbf{K}) = \mathcal{I}$, where $\mathcal{X}$ is the space of all scene-representation functions $\Phi$.
nodes.statement_clean: Theta maps a scene representation Phi together with camera extrinsics and intrinsics to a rendered image.

nodes.name: Surface Set $\Omega$
nodes.statement: $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ denotes the set of all points lying on the surface of the scene; geometry is implicitly represented as the level set where $\Phi$ transitions between feature vectors.
nodes.statement_clean: Omega is the implicit surface of the scene, defined as where the feature representation transitions between free space and matter.

nodes.name: Hypernetwork $\Psi$
nodes.statement: Mapping $\Psi : \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^l$, $\mathbf{z}_j \mapsto \Psi(\mathbf{z}_j) = \phi_j$, parameterized as an MLP with parameters $\psi$, that maps a latent code $\mathbf{z}_j$ to the parameter vector $\phi_j$ of the scene MLP $\Phi_j$.
nodes.statement_clean: Psi is a hypernetwork that turns a low-dimensional latent code into the parameters of an instance-specific scene MLP.

nodes.name: Latent Manifold Assumption
nodes.statement: Scenes of the same class are assumed to share shape and appearance properties characterizable by latent variables $\mathbf{z} \in \mathbb{R}^k$ with $k < l$, equivalently that all parameter vectors $\phi_j$ live in a $k$-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb{R}^l$.
nodes.statement_clean: The MLP parameters of all instances of one object class are assumed to live on a low-dimensional latent manifold.

nodes.name: Pixel Generator
nodes.statement: Per-pixel MLP that maps a single feature vector $\mathbf{v}$ at a ray-surface intersection to a single RGB color value; equivalent to a CNN with only $1\times 1$ convolutions.
nodes.statement_clean: A per-pixel MLP that converts feature vectors at intersection points to RGB colors, with no spatial convolutions.

nodes.name: Ray Parameterization
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{r}_{u,v}(d) = \mathbf{R}^T(\mathbf{K}^{-1}(u, v, d)^T - \mathbf{t})$ for $d > 0$, giving world coordinates of the point along the camera ray through pixel $(u,v)$ at distance $d$.
nodes.statement_clean: World-space ray parameterization for the camera ray through pixel (u,v) at depth d.

nodes.name: Joint Optimization Objective
nodes.statement: $\arg\min_{\theta, \psi, \{\mathbf{z}_j\}} \sum_{j=1}^M \sum_{i=1}^N \| \Theta_\theta(\Phi_{\Psi(\mathbf{z}_j)}, \mathbf{E}^j_i, \mathbf{K}^j_i) - \mathcal{I}^j_i \|_2^2 + \lambda_{dep} \| \min(\mathbf{d}^j_{i,\text{final}}, \mathbf{0}) \|_2^2 + \lambda_{lat} \| \mathbf{z}_j \|_2^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sum of image-reconstruction loss, depth-positivity regularizer, and Gaussian latent-code prior, jointly optimized over renderer, hypernetwork, and latent codes.

nodes.name: Few-Shot Reconstruction Objective
nodes.statement: $\hat{\mathbf{z}} = \arg\min_{\mathbf{z}} \sum_{i=1}^N \| \Theta_\theta(\Phi_{\Psi(\mathbf{z})}, \mathbf{E}_i, \mathbf{K}_i) - \mathcal{I}_i \|_2^2 + \lambda_{dep}\|\min(\mathbf{d}_{i,\text{final}}, \mathbf{0})\|_2^2 + \lambda_{lat}\|\mathbf{z}\|_2^2$, with $\theta, \psi$ fixed.
nodes.statement_clean: Latent-code-only optimization for new instances, holding the trained renderer and hypernetwork fixed.

nodes.name: Ray-Surface Intersection
nodes.statement: $\arg\min\; d \;\text{s.t.}\; \mathbf{r}_{u,v}(d) \in \Omega,\; d > 0$: find the smallest positive distance along the camera ray through pixel $(u,v)$ that lies on the scene surface $\Omega$.
nodes.statement_clean: Optimization problem of finding the closest ray-surface intersection along each camera ray.
assumptions: $\mathbf{r}_{u,v}(d)$ is the camera ray as in Eq.~\ref{eq:ray_param}

nodes.name: Scene Representation Learning
nodes.statement: Given a multi-instance dataset $\mathcal{D} = \{\mathcal{C}_j\}_{j=1}^M$ of posed-image collections, learn renderer parameters $\theta$, hypernetwork parameters $\psi$, and per-instance latent codes $\mathbf{z}_j$ to faithfully reconstruct images and discover shape/appearance priors.
nodes.statement_clean: End-to-end multi-instance scene representation learning from only posed 2D images.
conclusions: Learn $(\theta, \psi, \{\mathbf{z}_j\}_{j=1}^M)$ minimizing the objective in EP227.2

nodes.name: Differentiable Ray-Marching with RM-LSTM
nodes.statement: Iterative ray-marching algorithm that finds the world-coordinate ray-surface intersection by predicting an adaptive step length at each iteration via a learned RM-LSTM driven by the local scene feature $\Phi(\mathbf{x}_i)$.
output: World coordinates $\mathbf{r}_{u,v}(d_{\text{max\_iter}})$ of the estimated ray-surface intersection
nodes.pseudocode: Initialize $d_0 \gets 0.05$ (near plane), $(\mathbf{h}_0, \mathbf{c}_0) \gets (\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{0})$. For $i = 0$ to $\text{max\_iter}$: $\mathbf{x}_i \gets \mathbf{r}_{u,v}(d_i)$; $\mathbf{v}_i \gets \Phi(\mathbf{x}_i)$; $(\delta, \mathbf{h}_{i+1}, \mathbf{c}_{i+1}) \gets LSTM(\mathbf{v}_i, \mathbf{h}_i, \mathbf{c}_i)$; $d_{i+1} \gets d_i + \delta$. Return $\mathbf{r}_{u,v}(d_{\text{max\_iter}})$.

nodes.name: Sphere Tracing
nodes.statement: Classical ray-marching algorithm in which each step length equals the signed distance from the current point to the closest surface; the algorithm terminates at the surface where the signed distance is zero.
input: Signed distance field of the scene

nodes.name: Auto-Decoder Latent-Code Optimization
nodes.statement: Treat per-instance latent codes $\mathbf{z}_j$ as free variables and optimize them jointly with the network parameters by stochastic gradient descent, under a zero-mean diagonal-covariance Gaussian prior on $\mathbf{z}_j$.
output: Trained latent codes $\mathbf{z}_j$ jointly optimized with network parameters

nodes.name: SRN Joint End-to-End Training
nodes.statement: Stochastic gradient descent on the joint objective EP227.2 over renderer parameters $\theta$, hypernetwork parameters $\psi$, and latent codes $\{\mathbf{z}_j\}$, end-to-end without pre-training.

nodes.name: Few-Shot Reconstruction via Latent Optimization
nodes.statement: Given a trained model, freeze $\theta$ and $\psi$ and recover a latent code $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ for a new instance by minimizing the per-instance objective EP227.3 by SGD.
output: Latent code $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ representing the new instance

nodes.name: Shepard-Metzler Object Novel-View Synthesis
nodes.statement: Train SRNs and dGQN on 15 observations each of 1000 7-element Shepard-Metzler objects at $64\times 64$. SRNs reach $30.41$ dB PSNR on the training set vs $20.85$ dB for dGQN, $24.36$ dB vs $18.56$ dB in the two-shot setting, and $18.11$ dB vs $17.51$ dB in the one-shot setting.
nodes.statement_clean: Limited-data Shepard-Metzler experiment showing SRNs strongly outperform a deterministic GQN baseline.

nodes.name: Shapenet Cars and Chairs Novel-View Synthesis
nodes.statement: Train on 50 views per instance for $4.5$k chairs and $2.5$k cars from Shapenet v2 at $128\times 128$. SRNs achieve PSNR/SSIM of $26.23/0.95$ (chairs) and $26.32/0.94$ (cars) on training, outperforming TCO, WRL, and dGQN baselines in all 50-, 2-, and 1-shot settings.
nodes.statement_clean: Shapenet cars/chairs experiment where SRNs beat all three baselines across few-shot regimes.

nodes.name: Non-Rigid Face Model from Basel Faces
nodes.statement: Render 50 views each of 1000 faces from the Basel face model (224-dim parameter vector: 160 identity + 64 expression). SRNs conditioned on this disentangled latent space reconstruct face geometry/appearance and animate facial expression by varying the 64 expression parameters while holding identity fixed.
nodes.statement_clean: SRNs trained on Basel faces enable smooth animation of facial expressions while preserving identity.

nodes.name: Latent-Space Interpolation
nodes.statement: Interpolate between latent codes $\mathbf{z}_j$ of cars and chairs in Shapenet while rotating the camera; reconstructed scenes transition smoothly between models, demonstrating that the learned latent manifold is meaningful.
nodes.statement_clean: Linear latent-space interpolation produces smooth shape/appearance morphs between Shapenet instances.

nodes.name: Room-Scale Minecraft Scene
nodes.statement: Train a single SRN on 500 observations of a Minecraft room with multiple objects and four occluding columns; the model produces largely multi-view-consistent novel views and recovers occluding columns and object geometry, failing only on low-texture regions and thin tubes.
nodes.statement_clean: Single-scene SRN demonstration on a multi-object room-scale Minecraft environment.

nodes.name: Multi-View Consistency from Per-Pixel Generator
nodes.statement: Because the pixel generator is a per-pixel MLP, the same $(x,y,z)$ world coordinate always maps to the same color, so given correct ray-surface intersections the rendering is trivially multi-view consistent; 2D convolutions provide no such guarantee.

nodes.name: Fixed-Iteration Ray Marching
nodes.statement: The ray marcher uses a constant number of iterations rather than a dynamic termination criterion, since dynamic termination has no convergence guarantee while $\Phi$ and the RM-LSTM are still randomly initialized; depth maps from running estimates make the procedure interpretable.

nodes.name: Continuous vs Discrete Scene Representations
nodes.statement: $\Phi$ generalizes voxel grids and point clouds: it densely models scene properties at arbitrary resolution since it is continuous over $\mathbb{R}^3$, with effective resolution limited only by the MLP capacity.

nodes.name: Failure Modes
nodes.statement: The ray marcher may get stuck in surface holes or skim past occluders, causing the SRN to fill in or step through surfaces; objects far from the training distribution may match texture but fail to recover geometry; reconstructed depth maps make these failures diagnosable.

nodes.name: Loss-Term Roles
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{L}_{\text{img}}$ enforces image reconstruction in $\ell_2$, $\mathcal{L}_{\text{depth}}$ regularizes the positivity constraint $d > 0$ from EP227.1, and $\mathcal{L}_{\text{latent}}$ enforces the zero-mean Gaussian prior on $\mathbf{z}_j$.

nodes.name: Initialize Distance and LSTM State
nodes.statement: $d_0 \gets 0.05$ (near plane); $(\mathbf{h}_0, \mathbf{c}_0) \gets (\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{0})$ (LSTM hidden and cell states).

nodes.name: Iterative Marching Loop
nodes.statement: For $i = 0$ to $\text{max\_iter}$, repeat the following body: compute world coordinates from current depth, query feature, predict step length, and update depth.

nodes.name: Compute World Coordinates
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{x}_i \gets \mathbf{r}_{u,v}(d_i)$ using the ray parameterization (EP227.1).

nodes.name: Query Scene Feature
nodes.statement: $\mathbf{v}_i \gets \Phi(\mathbf{x}_i)$: extract the feature vector at the current ray position from the scene representation.

nodes.name: Predict Step Length via RM-LSTM
nodes.statement: $(\delta, \mathbf{h}_{i+1}, \mathbf{c}_{i+1}) \gets LSTM(\mathbf{v}_i, \mathbf{h}_i, \mathbf{c}_i)$: predict the next step length and propagate the LSTM state.

nodes.name: Increment Depth
nodes.statement: $d_{i+1} \gets d_i + \delta$: advance the ray by the predicted step length.

nodes.name: Return Final Intersection Estimate
nodes.statement: Return $\mathbf{r}_{u,v}(d_{\text{max\_iter}})$, the world coordinates of the estimated ray-surface intersection.

nodes.name: Initialize Parameters and Latent Codes
nodes.statement: Randomly initialize renderer parameters $\theta$, hypernetwork parameters $\psi$, and per-instance latent codes $\{\mathbf{z}_j\}_{j=1}^M$.

nodes.name: Forward Pass: Render Each Image
nodes.statement: For each $(j,i)$, build $\Phi_{\Psi(\mathbf{z}_j)}$ via the hypernetwork, run the differentiable ray marcher (AP227.1) to find intersections, and apply the pixel generator to produce the predicted image $\Theta_\theta(\Phi_{\Psi(\mathbf{z}_j)}, \mathbf{E}^j_i, \mathbf{K}^j_i)$.

nodes.name: Compute Joint Loss
nodes.statement: Evaluate $\mathcal{L}_{\text{img}} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{depth}} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{latent}}$ as in EP227.2 across the mini-batch.

nodes.name: SGD Update on $(\theta, \psi, \{\mathbf{z}_j\})$
nodes.statement: Backpropagate the joint loss end-to-end and apply a stochastic gradient step to $\theta$, $\psi$, and the latent codes $\mathbf{z}_j$ jointly.

nodes.name: Freeze Trained Parameters
nodes.statement: Hold renderer parameters $\theta$ and hypernetwork parameters $\psi$ fixed at their values from joint training (AP227.4).

nodes.name: Optimize New Latent Code
nodes.statement: Solve $\hat{\mathbf{z}} = \arg\min_{\mathbf{z}} \sum_{i=1}^N \| \Theta_\theta(\Phi_{\Psi(\mathbf{z})}, \mathbf{E}_i, \mathbf{K}_i) - \mathcal{I}_i\|_2^2 + \lambda_{dep}\|\min(\mathbf{d}_{i,\text{final}}, \mathbf{0})\|_2^2 + \lambda_{lat}\|\mathbf{z}\|_2^2$ via SGD.

nodes.name: Return Reconstructed Latent Code
nodes.statement: Return $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$, which fully specifies the new instance's scene representation $\Phi_{\Psi(\hat{\mathbf{z}})}$.
